passage:
A busy road near the school was dangerous. Students often crossed quickly between cars because the nearest traffic light was far away.
The school collected reports from students, parents, and teachers. They counted how many students crossed the road each morning. They also took pictures of the traffic.
The city office finally agreed to paint a new crossing and add a warning light.
On the first day, a teacher stood near the road and watched students cross safely. It seemed like a small change, but many families felt relieved.
The new crossing showed that complaints are stronger when they come with clear information. A safer street began with people carefully recording what they saw.
